data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A restricted backtracking search (DPLL-style) with 0-1 vector propagation can find a 44-comparator network for n=13 if one exists, because it systematically prunes the search space by detecting unsatisfiable partial networks.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The search space for n=13 with 44 comparators is vastly larger than for n=9/10, so it may be computationally intractable in a sandboxed Python environment within a reasonable time budget.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The heuristic for detecting 'unsatisfiable' partial networks might be too weak, leading to excessive backtracking.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If S(13) > 44, the search will exhaust all possibilities and fail, which is computationally expensive to prove.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Represent the network as a sequence of 44 comparators. Use depth-first search with the 0-1 principle: for each partial network of length k, test all 8192 binary vectors. If any vector reaches a state where the remaining 44-k comparators cannot possibly sort it (e.g., too many inversions remain for the available channels), backtrack. This exploits the fact that the 0-1 principle allows exact verification of partial networks.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
